findings.title: Rotation and emergency procedures target the wrong GitHub environment for the prod deploy and backup workflows
evidence: docs/SECRETS_ROTATION.md:5 — 'Secrets are stored as GitHub Environment Secrets (dev / prod scopes) and injected into the DO droplet .env file at deploy time by the deploy-do.yml workflow'
docs/SECRETS_ROTATION.md:173-176 — standard steps: `gh secret set SECRET_NAME --env dev` then `--env prod`
docs/SECRETS_ROTATION.md:191 — emergency: `gh secret set JWT_SECRET --env prod --body "new-emergency-secret,old-secret"`
docs/JWT_ROTATION.md:61-64 — prod secret location recorded as GitHub Environment `prod`
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:571 — the prod deploy job runs under environment `prod-approval` (dev uses `dev`), and reads all deploy secrets there (:578-637)
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:202 — prod Terraform apply uses `prod-approval`; :43 — plan uses `prod`
.github/workflows/db-backup.yml:14, db-restore-test.yml:14, storage-backup.yml:30 — backup jobs attach environment `dev` only
docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md:16-20,150-151 — states the prod deploy secrets 'must be available to prod-approval (scoped to it or repo-wide)' and that no reviewers are configured yet
findings.impact: An operator following the runbook sets the new value on `prod`, but the prod deploy job reads its secrets from `prod-approval`; GitHub environment secrets do not inherit, so the deploy keeps the old value and the rotation silently fails. The emergency JWT command therefore leaves the compromised value live in production. Backups read only `dev`, so a BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY rotation into `prod` is a no-op for the workflow that actually decrypts/encrypts.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the rotation/emergency steps to name the consuming environment per job (deploy + terraform apply → prod-approval; migrations/plan → prod; backups → dev), or make the prod secrets repo-wide and say so; add a post-rotation verification step (`gh secret list --env <env>`, then a deploy/run that proves the value landed) and a note that a value set on an environment the job does not use is a silent no-op.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d: repo evidence proves the documented environment does not match the consuming job's environment; live secret scoping is not inspectable from the repo (marked in Open Questions).

findings.title: Terraform plan artifacts carry sensitive variable values off the runner
evidence: .github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:66-95 — writes `$TF_ENV.tfvars` containing do_token, cloudflare_api_token, zone ids, admin_ip_ranges, droplet_size
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:124-135 — `terraform plan -out=tfplan`
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:154-159 — uploads the `tfplan` file as a workflow artifact (retention 1 day), downloadable by any user with repo read access
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:217-235 — the apply job downloads the same artifact and applies it
infra/terraform/digitalocean/variables.tf:1-5,41-45 — do_token and cloudflare_api_token are marked sensitive, which redacts CLI output only; plan files store variable values
.github/workflows/terraform-do.yml:138-152 — the PR plan-comment path is currently unreachable (workflow is manual/schedule only), so the exposure is the artifact, not comments
findings.impact: Anyone with repository read access (or a compromised collaborator session) can download the plan artifact while it exists and recover the DigitalOcean and Cloudflare API tokens, which are account-level credentials. This is the classic delivery-artifact secret leak path and is explicitly in this domain's extended checks.
findings.recommendation: Apply from the same protected job that plans (no artifact upload), encrypt the plan artifact, or move infra auth to short-lived OIDC credentials; if the artifact must stay, document the exposure and reduce retention. Add a CI check that no plan/tfvars artifact is uploaded unencrypted.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; Terraform plan-file contents asserted from Terraform semantics (not executed read-only). The workflow is manual-only, which lowers likelihood but not impact.

findings.title: JWT rotation runbook rotates the API verification copy, not the Supabase signing secret, and references a nonexistent JWT_EXPIRY
evidence: docs/JWT_ROTATION.md:4 — 'The first secret used for signing and all secrets accepted for verification'; docs/SECRETS_ROTATION.md:103,118-120 repeat this
apps/api/src/middleware/auth.ts:46-52,100-134 — the API only verifies HS256 tokens against the comma list, then falls back to Supabase auth.getUser
grep -rn 'jwt.sign' apps packages — no matches: no component in the repo signs JWTs
apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:113,143 — tokens are issued by Supabase (signInWithPassword → session.access_token); notifications.ts:83-101 re-verifies with the same list
docs/JWT_ROTATION.md:50 and docs/SECRETS_ROTATION.md:120 — 'default 24h (JWT_EXPIRY)'; grep JWT_EXPIRY finds only documentation (3 hits), no code/config key
docs/SECRETS_ROTATION.md:198 — force-logout step is 'clear Supabase auth sessions or rotate SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY' (rotating the service-role key does not invalidate user sessions)
findings.impact: Following the procedure changes only the API-side verification list; the Supabase project keeps signing with the old secret. During an emergency the compromised secret remains the signer, and while it stays in the comma list tokens signed with it are still accepted. The documented overlap window is also wrong because JWT_EXPIRY does not exist (the real lifetime is configured in Supabase).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the procedure around the Supabase project JWT secret: rotate it in the Supabase dashboard (invalidates sessions), keep the app comma-list only for the deploy overlap, remove the old value after the window, and verify that a token signed with the old secret is rejected. Replace JWT_EXPIRY with the actual Supabase token lifetime and document the concrete force-logout mechanism.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; code evidence is conclusive that the API does not sign and JWT_EXPIRY does not exist; operational impact assessed from the Supabase-hosted architecture.

findings.title: No automated `.env.example` ↔ runtime schema ↔ docs parity check
evidence: apps/api/src/config/env.ts:19-74 (38 keys), apps/worker/src/env.ts:5-43 (33 keys), apps/web/lib/env.ts:3-17 (13 keys)

docs/ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md has no ALERTMANAGER_*/NTFY_* rows (those live only in docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md:331-337)
findings.impact: The drift class that produced SECRET-P3-001 (worker template missing APP_BASE_URL) and the inventory gaps in SECRET-P2-001 can recur silently; nothing fails when a new schema key or workflow secret is added without docs/templates.
findings.recommendation: Add a dependency-free script to validate.yml that extracts keys from the three Zod schemas, the three .env.example files, and the docs tables, and fails on any mismatch; include workflow secrets.X against SECRETS_ROTATION.md.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; extends the previous runbook's proposed 'CI schema↔example↔docs parity check' to workflow secrets as well.

report:
# Environment and Secret Rotation Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: `repo-deep-dive`
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech` — read-only worktree `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8d`
- Generated at: 2026-10-11 (UTC)
- Auditor: domain subagent `38_env_secret_rotation` (area SECRET); read-only, no installs/builds/tests, no network
- Area code: SECRET
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/38_env_secret_rotation.md`
- Scope limitations: live GitHub environment/secret scoping, `gh secret list` timestamps, and droplet `.env`
  contents are not inspectable from the repository (marked `Unknown`); `gitleaks` is not installed on the
  audit host (deterministic lens DET-P3-001), so the committed scanner configuration was reviewed statically
  and with `grep` pattern checks instead of executed. Secret values were never printed; only names and
  `path:line` references appear.

## Scope

Reviewed at `8d299b8d`: the four `.env.example` templates; `docs/ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES.md`,
`docs/SECRETS_ROTATION.md`, `docs/JWT_ROTATION.md`, `docs/GITHUB_SECRETS_AND_VARIABLES_MATRIX.md`,
`docs/INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md`, `docs/DATA_BREACH_RESPONSE.md`; runtime validators (`apps/api/src/config/env.ts`,
`apps/worker/src/env.ts`, `apps/web/lib/env.ts`, `apps/api/src/lib/rls-startup-check.ts`); deploy/CI secret
handling (`deploy-do.yml`, `terraform-do.yml`, `build-push.yml`, `secret-scan` composite,
`secret-history-scan.yml`, `secret-rotation-reminder.yml`, backup workflows, `e2e.yml`); both compose files;
Terraform variables/artifacts; local dev scripts; `.gitignore`/`.dockerignore` exclusion rules; the previous
run's SECRET rows and the cross-domain rows whose subject matter is secret rotation/evidence.

Not reviewed: live GitHub environments and reviewers; the droplet and hosted Supabase; runtime logs; actual
secret values (never printed); the `_domains` outputs of sibling domains beyond cross-referencing.

## Evidence Reviewed

## Executive Summary

Secret handling at `8d299b8d` is materially stronger than at the previous full run. The API fails closed at
boot in production for PII encryption and CAPTCHA keys; the deploy pipeline forwards ~50 secrets as
environment variables (never interpolated into the remote script) and writes the droplet `.env` with mode
0600; the metrics token is written 0400 to the Prometheus container user; M365/Jira/JSM webhooks verify
credentials in constant time over raw bytes and fail closed with 501 when unconfigured; `JWT_SECRET` supports
comma-separated zero-downtime verification; diff secret scanning runs on PRs/pushes and a checksum-pinned
gitleaks job now scans full history weekly with a negative-fixture guard; and `.env.example` files match all
three runtime schemas.

The remaining risk is concentrated in the **documented rotation/revocation path**, not the runtime wiring:

1. **The rotation and emergency procedures target the wrong GitHub environment (P1).** `SECRETS_ROTATION.md`
   and `JWT_ROTATION.md` say `--env prod`, but the prod deploy job runs under `prod-approval` and the backup
   workflows run under `dev`; an operator following the runbook can rotate a value the consuming job never
   reads — silently, during an incident.
2. **The rotation inventory still lags the workflows (P2).** 20 secret names (including required
   `REDIS_PASSWORD`, today's `ALERTMANAGER_*`/`NTFY_ALERTS_*`, and the SSH host-key pins) are absent from the
   inventory; 13 are absent from the matrix.
3. **No exercised rotation evidence (P2/P3).** The Rotation Log has one undated "Initial deployment" row;
   the reminder workflow exists but no rotation or revocation drill artifact does.
4. **JWT rotation does not rotate the signer (P2).** The API only verifies; Supabase signs. The procedure
   rotates the API-side copy and references a `JWT_EXPIRY` key that does not exist.
5. **Delivery artifacts (P2).** The Terraform `tfplan` artifact embeds the DO/Cloudflare token values and is
   downloadable by any repo reader for its retention window.
6. **Break-glass is still undefined (P3).** No IT runbook, no escrow location, and `INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md`
   points at a `secret_rotation_runbook.md` that exists only inside an old audit-run folder (P2 doc defect).

Recommended next actions: fix the environment mapping in the rotation docs and add a post-rotation
verification step; reconcile the inventory/matrix with a CI parity check; run one real (dev) rotation drill
and record it; rewrite the JWT procedure around the Supabase signing secret; and either encrypt the tfplan
artifact or stop uploading it.

## Appendix

### A. Companion artifact — secret rotation runbook (summary; full text in Findings 13/16 and Recommendations)

1. **Scope:** every name in the inventory (once reconciled); values never pasted anywhere.
2. **Standard rotation:** generate at source → `gh secret set <NAME> --env <consuming-environment>` →
   deploy/verify → revoke old → record in the Rotation Log.
   - Consuming environments: deploy/app secrets → `prod-approval` (prod) / `dev`; migrations & Terraform
     plan → `prod` / `dev`; Terraform apply → `prod-approval`; backups → `dev`.
3. **JWT:** rotate the Supabase project JWT secret first; keep the comma-list only for the overlap window;
   after the window remove the old value and confirm an old-secret token is rejected.
4. **No-schedule keys:** `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and `BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` follow the re-encryption
   procedures in `SECRETS_ROTATION.md:62-99`; never rotate without a re-encrypt plan.
5. **Record:** date, secret names, operator, environment, incident flag, run URL.

### B. Companion artifact — emergency revocation plan (summary)

1. Revoke/disable the credential at the source first (provider console), preserving the audit trail.
2. Set the replacement with `gh secret set` into the **consuming** environment; redeploy the affected job.
3. If JWT/session material is involved: rotate the Supabase project JWT secret and invalidate sessions
   (concrete mechanism still to be documented — Open Question).
4. Rotate adjacent consumers (worker + API for Supabase keys; all consumers for shared integrations).
5. Run the full-history secret scan; record the incident and the rotation in the Rotation Log.
6. Break-glass rules: incident ticket + named approver, time-boxed, post-incident review.
